text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- U.S. denies talk of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu meeting Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
- 11 soldiers hurt in bus firebombing near Ramallah.
- Education Minister Zevulun Hammer appoints panel to probe school violence.
- Protest halts talk on Rabin conspiracy at Hebrew University.
- Majority supports Palestinian state, fears war - poll.
- Government posts surprising budget surplus in March. First quarter domestic deficit at 692 million shekels. Finance Minister Dan Meridor silent on extra cut.
- 1996 farm output growth almost stagnant.
- D-Pharm Ltd, an Israeli-based biotechnology firm, raises $6 million in private placement.
- Labour Minister Eli Yishai proposes relaxing closure for Palestinians who have held work permits over last five years.
GLOBES
- Meridor: Decision on budget cut to be influenced by slowdown.
- Managing director Erwin Eisenberg considers Israel Corp sale of Zim.
HAARETZ

- U.S. President Bill Clinton to make clear to Netanyahu: An accelerated final-state agreement will require meaningful concessions. It could be a freeze of settlements will be requested. U.S. to tell Arafat: Security coordination before progress on the peace process.
- Opposition leader Shimon Peres: Israel on the eve of war; unity government an urgent need.
- GNP in West Bank and Gaza fell 8.6 percent in 1996 -- stood at $1,700 per person last year compared with $16,500 per person in Israel.
- New arrest law would require detainees to be brought before a judge within 24 hours of detention; cell conditions to be improved.
- Parliamentary finance committee to discuss Arafat's secret account. Former finance minister Avraham Shohat: The money was openly transferred.
- Education ministry asks doctors to report to schools on students who carry AIDS virus.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu to submit to Clinton intelligence information on Palestinian Authority: "Arafat ordered his security chief Mohammad Dahlan not to cooperate in fight against terror."
- Surprise: 200 million shekel surplus in state budget in March.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- U.S. proposes deal: No to attacks, no to settlements.
